findings.description: The retryJob method uses unserialize() on database-stored payload data ($job->payload). An attacker with access to the failed_jobs table could inject arbitrary PHP objects, leading to remote code execution via PHP object injection/pop chain attacks.
findings.recommendation: Replace unserialize() with json_decode() for payload inspection, or use Laravel's built-in queue retry mechanisms (e.g., php artisan queue:retry) which handle deserialization safely in a controlled context.

findings.description: The show() method returns any report by ID without verifying the requesting user's agency owns the report. The report includes agency and user relationships, leaking cross-tenant data. Combined with line 53-57, this allows any authenticated user to read any report in the system.
findings.recommendation: Add authorization check: verify $report->agency_id === $request->user()->agency_id before returning data, or use Laravel's authorize() method with the ReportPolicy.

findings.description: The destroy() method deletes any report by ID without verifying ownership. Any authenticated API user can delete any report belonging to any agency by iterating report IDs.
findings.recommendation: Add agency ownership check before deletion: if ($report->agency_id !== $request->user()->agency_id) abort(404);

findings.description: GdprController only applies 'auth' middleware but not 'agency' middleware. This allows authenticated users who are not associated with any agency (or whose agency is inactive) to access GDPR data export/deletion endpoints, potentially manipulating consent records or export requests across agency boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Change middleware from ['auth'] to ['auth', 'agency'] to enforce agency context validation.

findings.description: The show() method returns role permissions for any roleId without verifying the role belongs to the requesting user's agency. This allows cross-tenant data leakage of role/permission structures.
findings.recommendation: Add agency scoping: verify the role belongs to $request->user()->agency_id before returning permissions.

findings.description: The destroy() method deletes any role by ID without verifying agency ownership. Any authenticated user with agency access can delete roles belonging to other agencies if they know/guess the roleId.
findings.recommendation: Add agency ownership validation in the deleteRole call or add a check at the controller level.

findings.description: The store() method accepts access_token from user input and stores it directly via mass assignment (spread operator). If the SocialAccount model's $fillable array is not properly restricted, an attacker could set arbitrary attributes like is_admin, agency_id, or other sensitive fields.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly list allowed fields in the create() call rather than using the spread operator. Verify the SocialAccount model has $fillable or $guarded properly configured.

findings.description: The restore() method accepts a filename parameter directly from the route without sanitization. An attacker could use path traversal sequences (../../etc/passwd) to restore from arbitrary files or access files outside the backup directory.
findings.recommendation: Validate filename against a whitelist pattern (e.g., alphanumeric with dashes/underscores only) and verify the file exists within the expected backup directory before processing.

findings.description: The handle() method passes $request->all() directly to the workflow engine without validation or sanitization. Malicious webhook payloads could inject unexpected data types, nested objects, or excessive payload sizes that may cause unexpected behavior in downstream workflow execution.
findings.recommendation: Add request validation to limit allowed fields, enforce size limits, and validate data types before passing to the workflow engine.

findings.description: The update() method allows any user with agency access to modify roles, but does not verify the user has permission to manage roles. Only owners/admins should be able to create/update/delete roles.
findings.recommendation: Add role-based authorization: verify the requesting user has 'role-management' permission or is an owner/admin before allowing role modifications.

findings.description: The store() method passes $request->filters and $request->columns directly to Report::create() without validation. These values could contain unexpected keys that get mass-assigned to the Report model if $fillable is not restrictive.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly validate and whitelist the filters and columns fields, or use $request->only() with explicit field lists before create().

findings.description: The export() method uses user-supplied filters without agency-scoping validation. An attacker could craft filters to extract data belonging to other agencies by manipulating filter conditions.
findings.recommendation: Always inject the agency_id filter from $request->user()->agency_id into the filter conditions before passing to the reporting service.

findings.description: The stats() method returns aggregate statistics about all agents across the system, including cost data and execution counts. This could reveal platform usage patterns and cost structures to any authenticated user.
findings.recommendation: Filter stats to only show data relevant to the user's agency, or restrict this endpoint to admin users.

findings.description: The OAuth redirect and callback endpoints do not have rate limiting applied. This could allow attackers to abuse OAuth flows for enumeration or force-authentication attacks.
findings.recommendation: Add throttle middleware to OAuth routes: ->middleware('throttle:10,1') for redirect and callback endpoints.

findings.description: The $query parameter is passed to the view without explicit length limits. While Blade's {{ }} syntax escapes output, excessively long query strings could cause rendering issues or be reflected in unexpected ways. The query is also used in SQL LIKE clauses which could be abused for wildcard-heavy searches.
findings.recommendation: Add max length validation to the query parameter ($request->validate(['q' => 'nullable|string|max:255'])) and consider rate limiting the search endpoint.
